thread:
sam: quick sanity check — for the internal control-plane APIs (routing policies, quota checks, rollout signals) are we leaning fully gRPC/proto-first or doing a JSON-on-the-edge gateway? need to align with console telemetry and rollout UX.
linh: my +1 is proto-first for the control-plane. strong typing helps with rollout signals and makes schema evolution explicit. also fewer mistakes in the policy language.
maria: agree on typing, but worried about console UX. ops folks use curl / browser tools. if the edge only speaks gRPC it's harder to debug without a shim.
jon: we should separate southbound (edge -> runtime) vs control-plane. southbound gRPC for perf, control-plane can be proto as well but expose JSON at gateway for web console & webhooks.
sam: that hybrid is what i was thinking. main questions: 1) how do we propagate per-route metadata for quotas/telemetry reliably across transcoders? 2) how do we version rollouts so console can show canary vs prod without extra translation layer?
linh: for metadata we can adopt an envelope header pattern: x-rd-route-metadata: base64(json) — keeps payloads unchanged and is language-agnostic. gateway decodes and surfaces it in console.
maria: envelope header sounds fine but watch header size limits for browsers/proxies. base64 JSON might get big if we include lots of labels.
jon: agree on size risk. alternate: keep route metadata minimal (route_id, rollout_tag, quota_bucket) and push detailed attrs to an async metadata service keyed by route_id. console fetches details when user drills in.
tara: +1 for async enrichment. console load needs to be fast; don't force every request to carry giant metadata. also helps with telemetry: we can store additional labels server-side for traces.
sam: ok so plan: keep runtime API small+typed (gRPC, proto) with a compact header for essential routing bits. gateway provides JSON facade and async metadata lookup for console drilldown.
linh: one more: quotas. enforcement should be colocated near the runtime for latency. but quota dashboards rely on aggregated counters that the gateway can more easily tag with customer-friendly ids.
maria: what if quota checks are two-stage: fast local allow based on counters (approx), then async strong check/charge at the gateway control plane? That gives low tail latency and consistent billing.
jon: two-stage sounds like eventual consistency tradeoff. we need SLA wording if we allow soft-allow then charge back. product needs to approve.
tara: ops perspective: console should expose both "observed" and "committed" usage metrics and a lag indicator. keep users informed about eventual adjustments.
sam: UX note: rollout view — console should visualize which routes are on canary, which model variants, and have a one-click rollback. to do that we need the control-plane API to include rollout metadata in a stable way.
linh: proto: add RolloutInfo { string tag; repeated string variants; enum phase { CANARY, ROLLING, GA } } and include a route_rollout field in RouteDescriptor proto. SDKs will generate nice types for UI.
maria: for gateway JSON we can expose a flattened shape: { route_id, rollout_tag, phase, variant } so front-end doesn't need to decode proto. keep mappings deterministic.
jon: telemetry: trace/span should carry route_id and rollout_tag. use deterministic sampling rules for canaries (100% capture for canary routes) so we can quickly detect regressions.
linh: note on traces: gRPC interceptors can populate span attributes easily. for JSON facade we must ensure the gateway maps headers -> span attrs.
maria: can we add a console feature: "investigate recent traces" that pre-filters by rollout_tag and shows latency / error diffs? product loves that.
tara: yes, and include a quota burn-down chart side-by-side so SREs can correlate throttles with increased errors.
sam: sounds good. last item: migration path — many teams still use JSON REST for older services. propose a compatibility mode: gateway accepts JSON and converts to proto for internal services, with a deprecation plan.
jon: deprecation plan should include metrics: % of requests using JSON over time, pages when > X% after Y months. rollout by tenants.
linh: implementation notes: build a small transcode lib in runtime to avoid duplicating logic across gateways. keep canonical proto as source-of-truth.
deploy-bot: deploy requested by @sam to infra-staging at next Wednesday 08:00 UTC — will run transcode smoketests and telemetry propagation checks.
sam: thanks. i'll draft an RFC for proto-first control-plane + JSON gateway facade + header envelope + async metadata service + two-stage quota model. will ping product/finance for billing/consistency texts.
maria: please include sample proto snippets and gateway mapping examples in the RFC.
sam: will do. quick code snippet i'll include in RFC:
```
message RouteDescriptor {
  string route_id = 1;
  RolloutInfo rollout = 2;
  repeated string quota_buckets = 3;
}
```
sam: ok ending thread — follow-ups in RFC. :thumbsup:
